docs.title: About polars-pairing
docs.text:
polars-pairing is a plugin that provides pairing functions to Polars. These functions encode a pair of natural numbers into a single natural number.

A pairing function performs a one-to-one mapping between (x, y) and i (represented by the circles in the Cartesian coordinate system). Figure by David Hagen.

This plugin implements six pairing functions (Hagen1, Szudzik2, Cantor3, Peter4, Rosenberg-Strong5, and Thotakura6), along with their corresponding unpairing functions, as Polars expressions. The pairing functions take two nonnegative integer columns as input and produce a single column containing the encoded pair. Conversely, the unpairing functions accept a single column as input and generate a struct column containing the values of the original pair.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
polars-pairing can be installed via Python's pip:

pip install polars-pairing

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
>>> import polars as pl
>>> import polars_pairing as plp

>>> df = pl.DataFrame({
...     "a": [1, 2, 38, 4],
...     "b": [5, 6, 77, 80]
... })
>>> df.select(plp.col("a").pairing.pair(plp.col("b")).alias("pair"))
shape: (4, 1)
┌──────┐
│ pair │
│ ---  │
│ u64  │
╞══════╡
│ 28   │
│ 40   │
│ 6006 │
│ 6408 │
└──────┘

>>> df.select(
...     plp.col("a")
...     .pairing.pair(plp.col("b"), method="hagen") # (1)!
...     .alias("hagen_pair"),
...     plp.col("a")
...     .pairing.pair(plp.col("b"), method="szudzik")
...     .alias("szudzik_pair"),
...     plp.col("a")
...     .pairing.pair(plp.col("b"), method="cantor")
...     .alias("cantor_pair"),
...     plp.col("a")
...     .pairing.pair(plp.col("b"), method="peter")
...     .alias("peter_pair"),
...     plp.col("a")
...     .pairing.pair(plp.col("b"), method="rosenberg_strong")
...     .alias("rosenberg_strong_pair"),
...     plp.col("a")
...     .pairing.pair(plp.col("b"), method="thotakura")
...     .alias("thotakura_pair"),
... )
shape: (4, 6)
┌────────────┬──────────────┬─────────────┬────────────┬───────────────────────┬────────────────┐
│ hagen_pair ┆ szudzik_pair ┆ cantor_pair ┆ peter_pair ┆ rosenberg_strong_pair ┆ thotakura_pair │
│ ---        ┆ ---          ┆ ---         ┆ ---        ┆ ---                   ┆ ---            │
│ u64        ┆ u64          ┆ u64         ┆ u64        ┆ u64                   ┆ u64            │
╞════════════╪══════════════╪═════════════╪════════════╪═══════════════════════╪════════════════╡
│ 28         ┆ 26           ┆ 26          ┆ 28         ┆ 26                    ┆ 24             │
│ 40         ┆ 38           ┆ 42          ┆ 41         ┆ 38                    ┆ 34             │
│ 6006       ┆ 5967         ┆ 6747        ┆ 6006       ┆ 5967                  ┆ 3194           │
│ 6408       ┆ 6404         ┆ 3650        ┆ 6409       ┆ 6404                  ┆ 3368           │
└────────────┴──────────────┴─────────────┴────────────┴───────────────────────┴────────────────┘

>>> df = pl.DataFrame({"p": [28, 40, 6006, 6408]})
>>> df.select(plp.col("p").pairing.unpair().alias("unpair")) # (2)!
shape: (4, 1)
┌───────────┐
│ unpair    │
│ ---       │
│ struct[2] │
╞═══════════╡
│ {1,5}     │
│ {2,6}     │
│ {38,77}   │
│ {4,80}    │
└───────────┘

>>> df = pl.DataFrame({"p": [26, 38, 5967, 6404]})
>>> df.select(
...     plp.col("p").pairing.unpair(method="szudzik").alias("unpair")
... ).unnest("unpair")
shape: (4, 2)
┌──────┬───────┐
│ Left ┆ Right │
│ ---  ┆ ---   │
│ u64  ┆ u64   │
╞══════╪═══════╡
│ 1    ┆ 5     │
│ 2    ┆ 6     │
│ 38   ┆ 77    │
│ 4    ┆ 80    │
└──────┴───────┘

>>> df = pl.DataFrame({"p": [28, 41, 6006, 6409]})
>>> df.select(
...     plp.col("p").pairing.unpair(method="peter").alias("unpair")
... ).unnest("unpair")
shape: (4, 2)
┌──────┬───────┐
│ Left ┆ Right │
│ ---  ┆ ---   │
│ u64  ┆ u64   │
╞══════╪═══════╡
│ 1    ┆ 5     │
│ 2    ┆ 6     │
│ 38   ┆ 77    │
│ 4    ┆ 80    │
└──────┴───────┘

>>> df = pl.DataFrame({"p": [26, 38, 5967, 6404]})
>>> df.select(
...     plp.col("p").pairing.unpair(method="rosenberg_strong").alias("unpair")
... ).unnest("unpair")
shape: (4, 2)
┌──────┬───────┐
│ Left ┆ Right │
│ ---  ┆ ---   │
│ u64  ┆ u64   │
╞══════╪═══════╡
│ 1    ┆ 5     │
│ 2    ┆ 6     │
│ 38   ┆ 77    │
│ 4    ┆ 80    │
└──────┴───────┘

>>> df = pl.DataFrame({"p": [24, 34, 3194, 3368]})
>>> df.select(
...     plp.col("p").pairing.unpair(method="thotakura").alias("unpair")
... ).unnest("unpair")
shape: (4, 2)
┌──────┬───────┐
│ Left ┆ Right │
│ ---  ┆ ---   │
│ u64  ┆ u64   │
╞══════╪═══════╡
│ 1    ┆ 5     │
│ 2    ┆ 6     │
│ 38   ┆ 77    │
│ 4    ┆ 80    │
└──────┴───────┘
  1. By default, the Hagen pairing function is used, but you can specify alternative functions. The available methods are: hagen, szudzik, cantor, peter, rosenberg_strong, and thotakura.
  2. The unpairing functions return a struct column containing the values of the original pair.

  1. Hagen, D. R. Superior Pairing Function. https://drhagen.com/blog/superior-pairing-function/ (2018). ↩

  2. Szudzik, Matthew. "An elegant pairing function." Wolfram Research (ed.) Special NKS 2006 Wolfram Science Conference. 2006. ↩

  3. Cantor, G. Ein Beitrag zur Mannigfaltigkeitslehre. Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik 1878, 242–258 (1878). ↩

  4. Péter, R. Rekursive Funktionen. Akadémiai Kiadó, Budapest (1951). ↩

  5. Rosenberg, A. L., and Strong, H. R. "Addressing arrays by shells." IBM Technical Disclosure Bulletin 14 (10), 3026–3028 (1972). ↩

  6. Thotakura, Manideep. "A New Bijective Pairing Alternative for Encoding Natural Numbers." Cryptology ePrint Archive (2025). https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1244. ↩

docs.text:

@pl.api.register_expr_namespace("pairing")
class PairingFunctions:
    def __init__(self, expr: pl.Expr):
        self._expr = expr

    def pair(
        self,
        other: IntoExpr,
        method: Method = "hagen",
    ) -> pl.Expr:
        """
        Applies a pairing function to uniquely encode two nonnegative integers
        into a single nonnegative integer. Null inputs give null outputs.

        Parameters
        ----------
        method
            The method to use for pairing. Either "hagen", "szudzik", "cantor",
            "peter", "rosenberg_strong" or "thotakura". Defaults to "hagen".

        Raises
        ------
        pl.exceptions.ComputeError
            If `method` is not a supported name, either input is neither an
            integer nor all-null, either input is negative or larger than the
            maximum UInt64 value, the encoded pair does not fit in a UInt64, or
            the two inputs have different lengths and neither has length 1.

        Examples
        --------
        >>> df = pl.DataFrame(
        ...     {
        ...         "n1": [2, 2, 3, 1501, None],
        ...         "n2": [6, 7, 8, 10740, 11],
        ...     }
        ... )
        >>> df.select(pl.col("n1").pairing.pair(pl.col("n2")).alias("pair"))
        shape: (5, 1)
        ┌───────────┐
        │ pair      │
        │ ---       │
        │ u64       │
        ╞═══════════╡
        │ 40        │
        │ 54        │
        │ 70        │
        │ 115350602 │
        │ null      │
        └───────────┘
        >>> df.select(
        ...     pl.col("n1").pairing.pair(pl.col("n2"), method="hagen").alias("hagen"),
        ...     pl.col("n1").pairing.pair(pl.col("n2"), method="szudzik").alias("szudzik"),
        ...     pl.col("n1").pairing.pair(pl.col("n2"), method="cantor").alias("cantor"),
        ...     pl.col("n1").pairing.pair(pl.col("n2"), method="peter").alias("peter"),
        ...     pl.col("n1").pairing.pair(pl.col("n2"), method="rosenberg_strong").alias("rosenberg_strong"),
        ...     pl.col("n1").pairing.pair(pl.col("n2"), method="thotakura").alias("thotakura"),
        ... )
        shape: (5, 6)
        ┌───────────┬───────────┬──────────┬───────────┬──────────────────┬───────────┐
        │ hagen     ┆ szudzik   ┆ cantor   ┆ peter     ┆ rosenberg_strong ┆ thotakura │
        │ ---       ┆ ---       ┆ ---      ┆ ---       ┆ ---              ┆ ---       │
        │ u64       ┆ u64       ┆ u64      ┆ u64       ┆ u64              ┆ u64       │
        ╞═══════════╪═══════════╪══════════╪═══════════╪══════════════════╪═══════════╡
        │ 40        ┆ 38        ┆ 42       ┆ 41        ┆ 38               ┆ 34        │
        │ 54        ┆ 51        ┆ 52       ┆ 54        ┆ 51               ┆ 42        │
        │ 70        ┆ 67        ┆ 74       ┆ 71        ┆ 67               ┆ 54        │
        │ 115350602 ┆ 115349101 ┆ 74937901 ┆ 115350603 ┆ 115349101        ┆ 57698282  │
        │ null      ┆ null      ┆ null     ┆ null      ┆ null             ┆ null      │
        └───────────┴───────────┴──────────┴───────────┴──────────────────┴───────────┘
        """
        return pl.plugins.register_plugin_function(
            args=[self._expr, other],
            kwargs={"method": method},
            function_name="pair",
            is_elementwise=True,
            plugin_path=lib,
        )

    def unpair(
        self,
        method: Method = "hagen",
    ) -> pl.Expr:
        """
        Applies an unpairing function to uniquely decode a nonnegative integer
        into two nonnegative integers. Null inputs give null outputs.

        Parameters
        ----------
        method
            The method to use for unpairing. Either "hagen", "szudzik", "cantor",
            "peter", "rosenberg_strong" or "thotakura". Defaults to "hagen".

        Raises
        ------
        pl.exceptions.ComputeError
            If `method` is not a supported name, the input is neither an
            integer nor all-null, or the input is negative or larger than the
            maximum UInt64 value.

        Examples
        --------
        >>> df = pl.DataFrame({"pair": [None, 607, 4, 18871362]})
        >>> df.select(pl.col("pair").pairing.unpair().alias("unpair"))
        shape: (4, 1)
        ┌─────────────┐
        │ unpair      │
        │ ---         │
        │ struct[2]   │
        ╞═════════════╡
        │ {null,null} │
        │ {24,15}     │
        │ {0,2}       │
        │ {513,4344}  │
        └─────────────┘
        >>> df.select(pl.col("pair").pairing.unpair(method="szudzik").alias("unpair"))
        shape: (4, 1)
        ┌─────────────┐
        │ unpair      │
        │ ---         │
        │ struct[2]   │
        ╞═════════════╡
        │ {null,null} │
        │ {24,7}      │
        │ {0,2}       │
        │ {1026,4344} │
        └─────────────┘
        """
        return pl.plugins.register_plugin_function(
            args=[self._expr],
            kwargs={"method": method},
            function_name="unpair",
            is_elementwise=True,
            plugin_path=lib,
        )
